thread:
maya: Heads up — after the 1.27.3 control plane upgrade in us-west-2 we saw two GPU node pools scale to 0 unexpectedly and CA isn't picking new nodes back up. Pods are stuck Pending with GPU resource requests.

samir: linking what I'm seeing here too. which cluster?

maya: cluster-2 (us-west-2). It looks like the node objects that came up from the new managed nodegroup are missing the node-template annotations CA relies on for group matching. Autoscaler-bot posted scale events: scaled-down to 0.

autoscaler-bot: Scale event: nodegroup gpu-pool-3 scaled from 2 -> 0 (policy: scaleDown). Reason: underutilized.

chris: do you have the kubectl describe for one of the affected node objects? curious which annotations dropped.

maya: pasted below — see annotations section, note missing cloud-provider templates we usually see.

```
Name: ip-10-0-3-44.ec2.internal
Labels: kubernetes.io/arch=amd64, kubernetes.io/hostname=ip-10-0-3-44
Annotations: kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket: /var/run/dockershim.sock
             node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable: false
# MISSING: node.openshift.io/node-group or cloudprovider/node-template-* annotations
```

kevin: hmm, earlier CA versions matched nodes to nodegroups by reading the node-template annotations our nodegroup controller sets. If the upgrade changed the node registration flow (e.g., cloud-controller-manager vX dropping annotations), CA can't associate the node with a group and treats it as unregistered capacity.

samir: I remember a similar regression where the node-authorizer path changed some annotation keys in 1.27. Could be a drift in the managed nodegroup bootstrap. Any cloud-controller-manager logs?

maya: grabbing logs now. Also saw this error in CA logs right before scale-down: `no matching node group for unclassified node ip-10-0-3-44`

```
W0412 14:02:13.123456       1 scale_down.go:341] No node group found for node "ip-10-0-3-44"; skipping
```

chris: ok that explains CA behavior. Two remediation paths: 1) ensure node bootstrap sets the expected annotations (hotfix via launch template/userdata or cloud provider) OR 2) temporarily pin CA to treat label-based matching (if supported) so it recognizes these nodes. Which is faster for prod?

kevin: short-term: manually patch the node objects with the expected annotations and then restart CA to force re-eval. Long-term: update nodegroup template in terraform so new nodes register correctly. We should also check if the 1.27 kubelet drop changed the annotation names.

maya: manual patch worked for one node — after adding `node.k8s.redwood/nodegroup: gpu-pool-3` CA reclassified it and canceled the scale-down. Pods started scheduling.

samir: good. Can you share the exact patch command so we can run a batch on the other nodes? And which annotations did you add?

maya: command we used: `kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-3-44 node.k8s.redwood/nodegroup=gpu-pool-3 --overwrite`
Annotations added: `node.k8s.redwood/nodegroup=gpu-pool-3` and `cluster-autoscaler.k8s.io/node-group=gpu-pool-3` (added both to be safe).

kevin: note — patching nodes prevents immediate scale-down but will leave idle GPUs running. cost FYI: each p4 instance is ~$X/hr. We should minimize manual patches and fix the root cause fast.

chris: filing a quick infra incident ticket and setting a short runbook: 1) patch current nodes 2) disable aggressive scaleDown window for GPU groups 3) revert any control-plane changes that broke node bootstrap if we find them 4) roll out corrected nodegroup config via terraform.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-048 — "Kube 1.27 node annotation regression affecting GPU autoscaling". Pager duty alerted to infra-oncall.

maya: follow-up: found a recent change in our node bootstrap script (kubelet-wrapper v2.3) that removed the `--register-with-taints` flag; that flag was responsible for injecting our nodegroup annotation. Rolling it back on a test pool now.

samir: nice catch. If rollback tests good, we should push terraform module change + update upgrade checklist to include verifying nodegroup annotations post-upgrade.

kevin: one more: check regional differences — only us-west-2 cluster-2 hit this; other clusters on same version fine. Probably a staged bootstrap rollout.

maya: confirmed — node bootstrap image v2026.03.10 deployed to us-west-2 yesterday during control plane migration. Staging and eu clusters still on older image.

chris: plan: 1) rollout bootstrap rollback to us-west-2 now (hotfix) 2) patch existing nodes with annotations (automation script) 3) increase CA scaleDown-delay for GPU groups to 30m to avoid flapping 4) postmortem and TF fix. Anyone object?

samir: +1, start hotfix. I'll help with the automation patch script.

maya: executing rollback playbook now. Will post updates in this thread. :mechanical_arm:

kevin: thanks all — please include cost estimate of the extra GPUs running in the incident ticket once we have numbers.

maya: rollback finished on test pool, nodes register with annotations again. Applying to prod pool now. expected impact minimal but I'll monitor CA logs for reclassification events.

chris: excellent. Keep monitoring. We'll leave this thread for the postmortem notes.
